unit.why: An anecdote told by the Gur rebbe: a case of a wife who secluded herself with another man is brought to the Seer of Lublin, who rules on it by halakhah and by his holy spirit.

stories.start_quote: סיפר הרה״ק מגור שפ"א בא לפני
stories.end_quote: בו שום דינר זהב. רמ"צ א"ז פי"ז אות י״ז
stories.summary_en: A case of a married woman who secluded herself with another man is brought to the Seer of Lublin; he permits the couple to live together as the law allows, and says that where only a stringency for the pious is at stake he can rely on his holy spirit, which shows him she was not defiled, but never where the law itself forbids.

quotes: כדין המבואר בסי' קע"ח ס״ו שאינה אסורה בלא קינוי
אבל כשאסורה מצד הדין אין לסמוך על הרוה״ק
tags.why: The story turns on a halakhic ruling and on how holy spirit relates to the law.

quotes: ענין שאשת איש נסתרה עם אחר
tags.why: Suspected adultery through seclusion is the case at issue.
Whether the wife is forbidden to her husband is the question decided.

quotes: נוכל לסמוך על רוה״ק שלי שאני רואה שלא נטמאה
tags.why: The Seer knows through his holy spirit that she was not defiled.
The couple's continued married life is the matter ruled on.
The wife's seclusion with another man triggers the case, but she does not act in the narrative.
The anecdote is framed as told by the Gur rebbe.
The tsaddik's holy spirit serves as a basis for a ruling, within limits.
A case is brought before the rebbe at his court.
